# 03-corewcf-service-host: Rehost TimeZoneConverterService on ASP.NET Core + CoreWCF (net10.0)

Migrate `src48/TimeZoneConverter` in place to `net10.0`, `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web` (`OutputType=Exe`), keeping `AssemblyName`/`RootNamespace` = `TimeZoneConvertor`. Replace the GAC references with `CoreWCF.Primitives` 1.9.1 and `CoreWCF.Http` 1.9.1 (no `CoreWCF.ConfigurationManager`). Add a `Program.cs` that registers the service, endpoints and behaviors in code. E1 is `BasicHttpBinding()` at `/TimeZoneConverter.svc`. E2 is `BasicHttpBinding(BasicHttpSecurityMode.Transport)`, active only where an HTTPS binding exists. M1 is `ServiceMetadataBehavior` with HTTP and HTTPS GET, and `includeExceptionDetailInFaults=false` is set explicitly (WCF-002/003/004). Remove the `.svc` file and its `Content`/`DependentUpon` items, `aspNetCompatibilityEnabled` (WCF-001; no HttpContext/System.Web use), `UseTaskFriendlySynchronizationContext`, IIS Express props and Web.config transforms. Map each effective Web.config setting to its new source per the inventory's behaviors/settings table. Move `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` to middleware, keep directory browsing off, and put `http://localhost:50355` in `launchSettings.json` so the SoapUI address stays the same. #skill:migrating-wcf-to-corewcf

Port the contract and extensibility code to `CoreWCF.*` namespaces with identical Name/Namespace/Action/ReplyAction/WrapperName/Order values. Split the server contract and wire types out of the generated `Contracts/ITimeZoneConverter.cs`, remove the unused `TimeZoneConverterClient` and the dead `<client>`/`<bindings>` config (WCF-007, D-4), and record that the file is now hand-maintained (SvcUtil regeneration no longer applies). Port `ResponseSerializerAttribute`/`ResponseDispatchFormatter`, the unused `RequestResponse*` pair (WCF-011) and the `XmlObjectSerializer` subclasses. **Highest risks:** whether CoreWCF applies an `IOperationBehavior` attribute placed on the implementation method and exposes `XmlSerializerOperationBehavior`/`DispatchOperation.Formatter` the same way (WCF-005), and preserving the hard-coded reply Action `"ConvertToOffset"` (WCF-006). Do not "fix" either. If attribute discovery differs, apply the behavior through `IServiceBehavior`/service-host configuration. Make sure the solution builds with a plain `dotnet build`/`msbuild` so `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` autobuild still works.

**Done when**: `TimeZoneConverter` builds on net10.0 with no `System.Web`/`System.ServiceModel` server references and no new warnings. Running locally, `POST /TimeZoneConverter.svc` with each SoapUI sample returns envelopes that match the golden baseline under Strict XML parity (Action, namespaces, element names and order, `xsi`/`xsd` prefixes, `<ToDateTime>` value). `?wsdl`/`?singleWsdl`/`?xsd` are served and match the baseline. E2 matches too, or is recorded UNVERIFIED if no HTTPS certificate exists. Every Web.config setting has a recorded destination or removal reason. The test project is expected not to build until task 04.

## Research findings (TaskExecutor, 2026-10-01, before any source edit)

**Decomposition verdict: atomic.** Evaluated scenario `execution.md` (Decomposition Rules → *small-cohesive-wcf* exception) and the `migrating-wcf-to-corewcf` skill decomposition section. One host, one service/contract/operation, 14 files, no unresolved design/security decision (E2 = conditional on an HTTPS binding, plan-decided), no independent deployment boundary; the format-only SDK checkpoint is not applicable (task 02 fallback explicitly folded the host's format change into this task). No scenario extensions apply at Execution scope.

### Confirmed current state (`src48/TimeZoneConverter`, HEAD e0c7aae)
- `TimeZoneConverter.csproj`: legacy WebApplication (`{349c5851…}`), `TargetFrameworkVersion v4.8.1`, `OutputType Library`, `AssemblyName`/`RootNamespace` `TimeZoneConvertor`, `LangVersion latest`, `OutputPath bin\`, IIS Express props (port 50355, `IISUrl http://localhost:50355/`, `IISExpressSSLPort` empty), `WcfConfigValidationEnabled`, `AutoGenerateBindingRedirects`; 18 GAC refs (System.ServiceModel, System.ServiceModel.Web, System.Web*, System.EnterpriseServices, …); `Content` .svc + Web.config; `Compile` 10 files (svc.cs `DependentUpon` .svc); `None` GenerateContracts.ps1 + Web.Debug/Release.config (`DependentUpon` Web.config); WebApplication.targets import. Stale wsdl/xsd items already removed in task 02.
- Source files: `TimeZoneConverter.svc` (activation only), `TimeZoneConverter.svc.cs` (service impl, `[ResponseSerializer]` on method), `ResponseSerializerAttribute.cs` + `ResponseDispatchFormatter.cs` (active), `RequestResponseSerializerAttribute.cs` + `RequestResponseDispatchFormatter.cs` (unused, WCF-011), `Contracts/ITimeZoneConverter.cs` (svcutil: interface + 4 wire types + `ITimeZoneConverterChannel` + unused `TimeZoneConverterClient`; fully-qualified `System.ServiceModel.*` attributes), `Contracts/TimeZoneConversionResponse.cs` (hand partial), `Serializers/ConvertToOffset{Request,Response}Serializer.cs` (`XmlObjectSerializer`, BCL-only — no change needed), `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs` (keep, `GenerateAssemblyInfo=false`), `GenerateContracts.ps1` (SvcUtil 4.8 regen script), `Web.config` + 2 transforms.
- Test project (net481 SDK-style) references the host and uses `TimeZoneConvertor.Serializers.ConvertToOffsetResponseSerializer`, `TimeZoneConverter.Contracts.{ConvertToOffsetResponse,TimeZoneConversionResponse}` → keep these namespaces/type names unchanged so task 04 only retargets.
- No HttpContext/System.Web/OperationContext use (WCF-001 removal is safe). No `[ServiceBehavior]`, no faults, sessions, security credentials.

### Packages / tools (verified)
- `CoreWCF.Primitives` 1.9.1 + `CoreWCF.Http` 1.9.1 present in global packages `Q:\.tools\.nuget\packages`; feed `azure-default` (packagefeedproxy) → HTTP 200; nuget.org disabled. .NET SDK 10.0.401, no global.json.
- Reflection of CoreWCF.Primitives 1.9.1: `CoreWCF.Description.IOperationBehavior` has the same 4 members incl. `ApplyClientBehavior(OperationDescription, CoreWCF.Dispatcher.ClientOperation)`; `XmlSerializerOperationBehavior` public; `DispatchOperation.Formatter/DeserializeRequest/SerializeReply` publicly settable; `ServiceContractAttribute.ConfigurationName` exists; `ServiceDebugBehavior.IncludeExceptionDetailInFaults` exists → the extensibility code ports by namespace swap only (WCF-005 code parity). Whether CoreWCF picks up the attribute from the implementation method is verified at runtime (custom serializer output = `<ToDateTime>` with offset + `xmlns:xsd`/`xmlns:xsi`; default formatter would emit UTC `ToDateTime` + `ToDateTimeOffset`). Fallback if not: apply via `IServiceBehavior`.

### Implementation plan (patterns to apply)
1. Project file → `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web`, `net10.0`, `OutputType Exe`, keep `AssemblyName`/`RootNamespace` `TimeZoneConvertor`, `LangVersion latest`, `GenerateAssemblyInfo false`, `Nullable` left disabled, `ImplicitUsings` disabled (explicit usings, minimal semantic drift); PackageReference CoreWCF.Primitives/Http 1.9.1. Drop GAC refs, ProjectTypeGuids, IIS Express props, WebApplication.targets, `WcfConfigValidationEnabled`.
2. Delete `TimeZoneConverter.svc` (WCF-002), `Web.config`, `Web.Debug.config`, `Web.Release.config` (settings mapped below; Sdk.Web publish generates the ANCM web.config), `GenerateContracts.ps1` (SvcUtil 4.8 would regenerate `System.ServiceModel` code over the hand-maintained CoreWCF contract; original kept at `wcf-baseline/contracts-original/ITimeZoneConverter.cs` and in git history).
3. Split `Contracts/ITimeZoneConverter.cs`: interface only (CoreWCF attributes, identical Namespace/ConfigurationName/Action/ReplyAction, `XmlSerializerFormat`); wire types to `Contracts/TimeZoneConverterMessages.cs` (TimeZoneConversionRequest, TimeZoneConversionResponse partial, ConvertToOffsetRequest/Response message contracts with identical WrapperName/WrapperNamespace/IsWrapped/MessageBodyMember Namespace+Order and XmlType/XmlElement Order); remove `ITimeZoneConverterChannel` + `TimeZoneConverterClient` (WCF-007, D-4). Header records hand-maintained status.
4. Port 4 extensibility files `System.ServiceModel.*` → `CoreWCF.*` (logic byte-identical, incl. hard-coded reply Action `"ConvertToOffset"` — WCF-006).
5. `Program.cs`: `AddServiceModelServices()`, `AddServiceModelMetadata()`; X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN middleware; `UseServiceModel`: `AddService<TimeZoneConverterService>` (+ `ServiceDebugBehavior.IncludeExceptionDetailInFaults=false` explicitly), E1 `BasicHttpBinding()` at `/TimeZoneConverter.svc`, E2 `BasicHttpBinding(Transport)` (Name `BasicHttpsBinding` to mirror WCF basicHttpsBinding port naming) only when the host has an HTTPS binding (urls / https_port(s) / Kestrel endpoints config); `ServiceMetadataBehavior` HttpGet+HttpsGet.
6. `Properties/launchSettings.json` with `applicationUrl http://localhost:50355` (Kestrel profile + IIS Express profile, sslPort 0 = same as original).
7. Validate: `dotnet build` (0 warnings), run via launch profile, re-run `wcf-baseline/Capture-WcfWireBaseline.ps1` to a new output dir under this task folder, compare byte-for-byte/XML-canonically with golden; E2 metadata structure via an http+https run using only the existing dev cert (no TLS bypass → E2 wire UNVERIFIED).

### Web.config setting → destination map
| Setting | Destination / disposition |
|---|---|
| `appSettings aspnet:UseTaskFriendlySynchronizationContext=true` | removed — ASP.NET-only, no SynchronizationContext in ASP.NET Core |
| `system.web compilation debug/targetFramework`, `httpRuntime targetFramework` (+ transforms) | removed — not applicable (precompiled ASP.NET Core) |
| `bindings/basicHttpBinding BasicHttpBinding_ITimeZoneConverter` + `<client>` endpoint | removed — dead client config (WCF-007/D-4) |
| `serviceMetadata httpGetEnabled/httpsGetEnabled=true` | `Program.cs` `ServiceMetadataBehavior` (WCF-004) |
| `serviceDebug includeExceptionDetailInFaults=false` | `Program.cs` `ServiceDebugBehavior` explicitly false (WCF-004) |
| `protocolMapping https→basicHttpsBinding` | `Program.cs` E2 conditional explicit endpoint (WCF-003) |
| `serviceHostingEnvironment aspNetCompatibilityEnabled=true` | removed — WCF-001, no code dependency |
| `serviceHostingEnvironment multipleSiteBindingsEnabled=true` | host URLs (launchSettings/`urls`/Kestrel/IIS bindings); CoreWCF builds base addresses from server addresses |
| `system.webServer modules runAllManagedModulesForAllRequests` | removed — IIS integrated-pipeline module setting, no ASP.NET Core equivalent needed |
| `httpProtocol customHeaders X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` | `Program.cs` middleware |
| `directoryBrowse enabled=false` (Debug transform true) | preserved: ASP.NET Core has no directory browsing unless `UseDirectoryBrowser` (not added) |
| `.svc` `Debug="true"` | removed — not applicable |

### Outcome note (post-execution)
- Deviations from the plan above: (a) `OperationDescription.Behaviors.Find<T>` → `OperationBehaviors.OfType<T>().FirstOrDefault()` (CoreWCF API surface); (b) `ConvertToOffsetResponseSerializer` namespace insertion order swapped to restore Framework wire order `xmlns:xsd` before `xmlns:xsi` (.NET XmlSerializerNamespaces is insertion-ordered). Details/evidence: progress-details.md.
